headline: No significant rainfall impacts across England and Wales, with extreme heat the dominant operational hazard.
summary:
Over the past 24 hours, rainfall across England and Wales has been light and patchy, with the highest gauge total only 7.0 mm at Herne Bay in SE England; other notable totals were 6.2 mm at Mersea, 6.0 mm at Broadstairs and 5.6 mm at Holland Park. Regional mean totals were low, at 1.4 mm in SE England and 0.8 mm or less elsewhere, with no gauge exceedances of 10 mm in 1 hour or 30 mm in 1 hour. Radar composites show very limited precipitation over England and Wales overnight, consisting mainly of isolated weak echoes over parts of the Midlands, south Wales, south-west England and the far south-east, with more organised showers remaining offshore to the west of Ireland and near the Channel. The 24-hour accumulation map supports a scattered, localised distribution rather than widespread rain, with the most persistent light falls focused in parts of Kent, Essex, London and adjacent south-eastern counties.

There are no active Met Office rain or thunderstorm warnings and no named storms affecting England and Wales; the only active warnings are for extreme heat, including an amber warning across much of England and Wales and a red extreme heat warning from 08:00 UTC today to 20:00 UTC on 25 June for parts of the Midlands, East of England, South West England, Wales and London and the South East. Rapid Flood Guidance is not active, and Flood Guidance Statement data are not available in this dataset. No rainfall intensity thresholds have been exceeded in the gauge network, so there is currently no evidence of heavy rainfall at or above 10 mm in 1 hour, nor any extreme short-duration rainfall at or above 30 mm in 1 hour. Antecedent soil moisture data are not provided, but the very low recent rainfall totals imply no broad wet-ground signal from the last 24 hours across England and Wales.

UKV regional accumulation tables are not available, so no quantified 6-, 12-, 24- or 48-hour rainfall totals can be stated from the supplied forecast dataset. The MSLP analyses at 05:00 UTC and 06:00 UTC show weak pressure gradients across England and Wales, with a 1020 mb high to the west near Ireland and shallow lows to the east and south-east, a pattern consistent with slack, hot and humid conditions rather than organised frontal rainfall. Given the near-absence of current rain on radar over England and Wales and the lack of forecast accumulation data, no specific area of significant rainfall concern can be identified from the supplied information for the outlook period. Any precipitation signal remains isolated and slight at this time, with no evidence in the provided data of a peak rainfall episode over England and Wales.
